extracted.intended_audience: railroads and railroad industry stakeholders, regulatory compliance officers, agency counsel, and other regulated entities and their advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Final rulemaking document from the Federal Railroad Administration making administrative updates to 49 CFR part 234 (grade crossing safety), including amendments to penalty language, address updates, and regulatory analyses explaining exemptions from notice-and-comment and other legal assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of change — administrative updates
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule makes administrative updates to FRA's grade crossing safety regulations, including updating addresses in those regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary states changes are 'miscellaneous, administrative updates' to 49 CFR part 234, such as updating web addresses and replacing obsolete references; no substantive policy changes intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective [July 1, 2025].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule must specify an effective date; this document sets July 1, 2025 as the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend §234.6(a) — replace specific penalty amounts with general references
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA is amending §234.6(a) by replacing references to specific penalty amounts with general references to the minimum civil monetary penalty, ordinary maximum civil monetary penalty, and aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are referred to 49 CFR part 209, appendix A for the statutorily provided civil penalty amounts (updated for inflation); the amendment also updates the FRA web address from www.fra.dot.gov to https://railroads.dot.gov/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update statutory reference for definition of 'person'
rubrics_metrics.description: To be consistent with other definitions of 'person,' FRA is updating the reference in the parenthetical from 1 U.S.C. 1 to 49 U.S.C. 21301.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change aligns cross-references within CFR definitions to current statutory citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA waiver for rules of agency organization/procedure/practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), an agency may waive the normal notice and comment procedures if the action is a rule of agency organization, procedure, or practice (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency invokes this provision for purely administrative changes that modify organization/procedure/practice and that would not benefit from public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA good-cause waiver (no notice-and-comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the APA, an agency may waive notice and comment procedures when the agency for good cause finds that notice and public procedure are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA finds notice and comment unnecessary here because the final rule merely makes miscellaneous administrative updates (e.g., updating web addresses) that would not benefit from public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalty applicability and per-violation structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (entities covered under 49 U.S.C. 21301, including railroads; managers, supervisors, officials, employees or agents of a railroad; owners, manufacturers, lessors, lessees of railroad equipment, track, or facilities; independent contractors; and their employees) who violates any requirement of this part (except §234.11) or causes such violation is subject to a civil penalty of at least the minimum civil monetary penalty and not more than the ordinary maximum civil monetary penalty per violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each day a violation continues is a separate offense; FRA's website contains a schedule of civil penalty amounts (see 49 CFR part 209, appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual liability limited to willful violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties may be assessed against individuals only for willful violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits individual penalties to cases showing willfulness; corporate/entity penalties operate under the broader per-violation scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravated maximum penalty conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A penalty not to exceed the aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty per violation may be assessed where: a grossly negligent violation, or a pattern of repeated violations, has created an imminent hazard of death or injury to persons; or a death or injury has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggravated maximum applies in circumstances involving gross negligence, repeated violations creating imminent hazard, or actual death/injury; see cross-reference to 49 CFR part 209, appendix A for amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railroad non-responsibility for variances beyond control (due diligence exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The railroad is not responsible for compliance with respect to any condition inconsistent with the technical standards set forth in this part where such variance arises as a result of actions beyond the control of the railroad and the railroad could not have prevented the variance through the exercise of due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sentence does not excuse noncompliance resulting from actions of the railroad's employees, agents, or contractors; due diligence is the limiting standard for excusing responsibility when variance arises beyond railroad control.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB/E.O. 12866 significance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA/OMB) determined that this final rule is not a significant regulatory action under section 3(f) of E.O. 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because changes are administrative (e.g., replacing specific penalty figures with references, updating web addresses), the rule is found not to impose additional burdens and may provide qualitative clarifications to regulated entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 14192 deregulatory-action identification
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 14192 requires that for each new regulatory action issued, at least ten prior regulations be identified for elimination; implementation guidance defines two types of E.O. 14192 actions. An E.O. 14192 deregulatory action is defined as 'an action that has been finalized and has total costs less than zero.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA states this final rule is expected to have total costs less than zero and therefore would be considered an E.O. 14192 deregulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) exemption where notice and comment is waived
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA and E.O. 13272 require an agency to prepare and make available a regulatory flexibility analysis describing the effect on small entities; a regulatory flexibility analysis is not required when a rule is exempt from notice and comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA determined the rule is exempt from notice and comment, and thus a regulatory flexibility analysis is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — no new information collection
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule contains no new information collection requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency explicitly states the rule offers regulatory flexibilities and does not create new PRA burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA analysis — categorical exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA has determined that this rule is categorically excluded pursuant to 23 CFR 771.118(c)(4), '[p]lanning and administrative activities that do not involve or lead directly to construction, such as: [p]romulgation of rules, regulations, and directives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency concludes the rulemaking will not result in environmental impacts and no unusual/extraordinary circumstances are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism implications assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule will not have a substantial effect on the States, on the relationship between the national government and the States, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities among levels of government; in accordance with E.O. 13132, preparation of a Federalism Assessment is not warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule materially affected federal-state relations, a Federalism Assessment would be needed; FRA concludes none is warranted here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule will not result in aggregate expenditures of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) in any one year by state, local, or tribal governments, or the private sector; thus, consistent with UMRA section 202, FRA is not required to prepare a written statement detailing such effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment threshold for UMRA not met; therefore no UMRA statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy impact (E.O. 13211) — not significant
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA evaluated this rule under E.O. 13211 and determined that it is not a 'significant energy action' within the meaning of that order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rule were a significant energy action, a Statement of Energy Effects would be required; FRA concluded it is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation (E.O. 13175) — not required
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA evaluated this final rule under E.O. 13175 and determined it would not have a substantial direct effect on Indian tribes, would not impose substantial direct compliance costs on tribal governments, and would not preempt tribal laws; therefore, tribal consultation and a tribal summary impact statement are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rule affects tribes directly, consultation requirements and summary impact statements apply; FRA concluded none of those conditions exist here.

rubrics_metrics.name: International trade impact assessment / Trade Agreement Act consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trade Agreement Act of 1979 prohibits Federal agencies from engaging in standards or related activities that create unnecessary obstacles to foreign commerce; this rulemaking is purely domestic in nature and is not expected to affect trade opportunities for U.S. firms or foreign firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency notes legitimate domestic objectives (e.g., safety) are not considered unnecessary obstacles; international standards consideration applies where appropriate, but not here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document drafting and amendment format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Rule includes authority citation, specific amendatory language altering the Code of Federal Regulations (e.g., 'Revise §234.6(a) to read as follows:'), list of subjects, issuance signature, FR Doc filing line, and billing code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule documents must include standard metadata and amendatory text so that CFR editors and the public can identify legal authority, specific regulatory text changes, and administrative provenance (issuer, signature, FR Doc number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation status, docket, and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are no longer being accepted; Docket No. FRA-2025-0101; supporting documents: none available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document records public participation windows (closed), docket identifiers for Regulations.gov, and whether supporting documents are posted; practitioners should consult the docket and PDF on govinfo.gov for the official electronic format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references and external citations requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule references and relies on various Executive Orders, statutes, OMB memoranda, and other CFR parts (e.g., E.O. 12866, E.O. 14192, RFA, PRA, NEPA, 49 CFR part 209 appendix A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules commonly include footnotes and citations to governing statutes, executive orders, and implementing guidance; readers should follow those citations for procedural and substantive context.
